name: InterStim pivotal trials
question: Does sacral nerve stimulation improve refractory urinary urge incontinence compared with delayed implantation and continued standard therapy?

arms.label: Immediate InterStim sacral nerve stimulation (six-month diary set)
Delayed implantation with standard medical therapy (six-month diary set)

design.population: 155 enrolled with refractory urinary urge incontinence; 98 positive test-stimulation responders randomized, with 6-month diaries from 34 immediate-implant and 42 delayed-implant patients.
design.description: Prospective, multicenter, open-label superiority randomized trial; arm counts shown are the interim six-month diary analysis set.
design.locator: Full text, Results and Table 2, p 354

verdictNote: All three primary diary measures met the interim significance threshold in the 76-patient analysis.
takeaway: Among test-stimulation responders, immediate InterStim versus delayed implantation reduced urge-incontinence episodes, severity and pad use at six months in 76 patients with diaries (all between-group P < 0.0001); 98 were randomized.

reports.label: Urge-incontinence randomized report
reports.citation: Schmidt RA, Jonas U, Oleson KA, et al. "Sacral nerve stimulation for treatment of refractory urinary urge incontinence." *J Urol.* 1999;162(2):352-357. doi:10.1016/S0022-5347(05)68558-8
reports.followUp: 6 months randomized comparison in 76 patients with diaries; implanted cohort followed up to 18 months in reported table
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Results and Tables 2-3, pp 354-355

results.measure: Baseline to 6 months in the interim diary analysis
results.note: Between-group ordered logistic regression P < 0.0001; interim adjusted threshold 0.0005 in Methods.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Figure 2, p 354

results.measure: Baseline to 6 months in the interim diary analysis
results.note: Severity uses a logarithmic rank: 1 mild, 2 moderate, 3 heavy; between-group P < 0.0001.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Figure 3, p 354

results.measure: Baseline to 6 months in the interim diary analysis
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Figure 4, pp 354-355

results.measure: Dry at 6 months among immediately implanted patients
results.note: A further 10/34 (29%) had more than 50% fewer episodes; these 34 are the six-month immediate-arm diary set.
results.locator: Full text, Results and Figure 2, p 354

results.measure: Dry or at least 50% fewer any leaking episodes at 18 months after implant
results.note: Uncontrolled implanted follow-up; the paper prints a percentage but no success numerator.

harms.label: Pulse-generator site pain
harms.note: Pooled safety set of 157 implants across urge incontinence, urgency-frequency and retention; 12-month probability was not reported for this item.

harms.label: Implant-site pain
harms.note: Pooled safety set of 157 implants across three indications; site pain is separate from generator-site pain.

harms.label: Lead migration
harms.note: Pooled safety set of 157 implants across three indications.

harms.label: Surgical revision for complication
harms.locator: Full text, Safety and Table 4, p 355
harms.note: 51/157 implanted patients; 72 revision events and 76 surgeries. Table 4 includes 6 permanent explants, 4 temporary explants with reimplantation, 14 device-exchange patients, 16 lead/extension-reposition patients and 23 generator-reposition patients.

harms.label: Explantation for complication

values.exp: 6/157 permanent explants (3.8%); 4/157 temporary explants with reimplantation (2.5%)

harms.note: Reasons for permanent explant: implant-site pain (3), infection (2), bowel-function change (1); temporary explant: infection (2), implant-site pain (1), material allergy (1). Categories are not mutually exclusive.

harms.label: Infection requiring explantation

values.exp: 4 infection-attributed explant events: 2 permanent and 2 temporary (pooled safety set n=157)

harms.locator: Full text, Safety and Table 4, p 355
harms.note: The text combines infection or skin irritation as 5.7%, but Table 4 attributes four explant events specifically to infection; no infection-only denominator is printed.

delivery.label: Delayed implantation
delivery.value: After 3–7 days of test stimulation and greater than 50% symptom improvement, 98/155 enrolled patients were randomized; 42 patients in the six-month delay-group diary analysis received standard medical therapy and were then offered implantation.
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 353; Results, p 354

delivery.label: Stimulation deactivation
delivery.value: Among 52 implanted patients completing a six-month on/off test, turning stimulation off for at least 3 days increased mean episodes/day from 2.9 to 9.5, severity rank from 0.8 to 1.9 and pad use/day from 1.2 to 5.8 (all P < 0.0001).
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 353; Results, p 354

delivery.label: Permanent implant technique
delivery.value: A multiprogrammable neurostimulator was placed in a subcutaneous pocket, typically in the lower abdominal quadrant; the lead was positioned along the target sacral nerve and anchored.
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 353

reports.label: Urgency-frequency randomized report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed and Crossref, June 2000 issue; day imputed
reports.citation: Hassouna MM, Siegel SW, Lycklama à Nÿeholt AAB, et al. "Sacral neuromodulation in the treatment of urgency-frequency symptoms: a multicenter study on efficacy and safety." *J Urol.* 2000;163(6):1849-1854. doi:10.1016/S0022-5347(05)67558-1
reports.followUp: 6 months randomized; implanted patients followed to 24 months
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 1849; Tables 4-5, p 1853

results.measure: Voids per day, baseline to 6 months in immediate-implant group
results.note: Prespecified interim alpha for primary diaries was 0.01; between-group ordered logistic regression P < 0.0001.
results.locator: Full text, Results and Figure 1, pp 1850-1851

results.measure: mL per void, baseline to 6 months in immediate-implant group
results.note: Prespecified interim alpha was 0.01; between-group ordered logistic regression P < 0.0001; Table 2 also prints P=0.001 for the mean comparison.
results.locator: Full text, Table 2 and Figure 2, pp 1851-1852

results.measure: Urgency rank, baseline to 6 months in immediate-implant group
results.note: Urgency rank: 0 none, 1 mild, 2 moderate, 3 severe; prespecified interim alpha was 0.01. Table 2 prints P=0.01 for the mean comparison; the text reports P < 0.0001 for the primary diary comparison.

results.endpoint: Clinical success for urgency before void
results.measure: Higher voided volume with same or reduced urgency at 6 months
results.note: Clinical-success definition differs from the primary mean urgency rank comparison.

harms.label: Pooled implant adverse events and revision

values.exp: 219 implanted across three indications; 12-month event probabilities: generator-site pain 15.3%, new pain 9.0%, suspected lead migration 8.4%, infection 6.1%, electric shock 5.5%, lead-site pain 5.4%; revision in 33.3%

harms.note: These are pooled rates, not the 25-person urgency-frequency immediate arm; numerator counts and a rate denominator for each event are not printed.

delivery.label: Test and implant
delivery.value: All 51 randomized patients had at least 50% improvement in primary diary parameters during a 3–7-day percutaneous S3 and/or S4 test; 25 received immediate implantation and 26 standard therapy with delayed implantation after 6 months.
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 1850

delivery.label: Implant components and on/off test
delivery.value: The implant comprised a subcutaneous neurostimulator, a lead adjacent to the target sacral nerve and an extension. At 6 months, 22/25 immediate-arm patients underwent deactivation; 1 had an explant and 2 declined the test.
delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 1850; Results, p 1851

reports.label: Retention randomized report
reports.dateLocator: PubMed and Crossref, January 2001 issue; day imputed
reports.citation: Jonas U, Fowler CJ, Chancellor MB, et al. "Efficacy of sacral nerve stimulation for urinary retention: results 18 months after implantation." *J Urol.* 2001;165(1):15-19. doi:10.1097/00005392-200101000-00004
reports.followUp: 6 months randomized; effectiveness sustained through 18 months after implantation
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Study Design and Methods, p 16; Results, p 17

results.measure: Catheterized residual volume per catheterization, baseline to 6 months, diary completers
results.note: Two-sample t test of mean changes, prespecified significance P=0.05; 29/37 immediate and 22/31 control patients supplied six-month diaries.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 16; Table 2, p 18

results.note: Success means no catheterization or at least 50% less catheterized volume per catheterization. Numerators are reconstructed from the rounded percentages and the 29/22 diary analysis sets; the paper prints percentages, not these counts.
results.locator: Full text, Abstract, p 15; Results, p 16; Table 2, p 18

results.measure: No catheterization at 6 months among implanted patients
results.note: A further 4/29 (14%, inferred) reduced catheterized volume per catheterization at least 50%; these counts derive from rounded percentages and the 29-patient diary set.
results.locator: Full text, Abstract, p 15; Results, p 16; Table 2, p 18

results.measure: No catheterization or at least 50% lower catheterized volume per catheterization at 18 months

values.exp: 17/24 (71%); 14/24 (58%) no catheterization and 3/24 (13%) at least 50% lower volume

results.note: 21 supplied an 18-month diary; three earlier withdrawals (two for lack of efficacy, one for adverse event) were counted as failures. No concurrent control remained.
results.locator: Full text, Results and Discussion, p 17

harms.label: Pooled implant adverse events

values.exp: 219 implants across three indications; 12-month probabilities: generator-site pain 15.3%, new pain 9%, suspected lead migration 8.4%, infection 6.1%, electric shock 5.5%, lead-site pain 5.4%

harms.locator: Full text, Implant safety and benefit, p 17
harms.note: Pooled across indications; the paper does not report retention-arm event numerators or denominators for these rates.

delivery.label: Screening and allocation
delivery.value: 177 retention patients underwent 3–7-day percutaneous test stimulation; 68/177 (38.4%) met the greater than 50% improvement criterion and were randomized (37 immediate implant, 31 delayed implant).
delivery.locator: Full text, Study Design and Methods and Results, p 16

delivery.label: Six-month diary availability
delivery.value: At six months, 29/37 immediate-implant and 22/31 control patients supplied diaries; among the other 17, 6 had not yet reached six months, 3 were lost to follow-up and 8 did not submit a diary.

delivery.label: Reprogramming
delivery.value: Among 48 implanted patients with six-month device data, mean reprogrammings were 3.9 (range 1–14).

reports.label: Five-year implanted cohort

harms.label: Device- or therapy-related adverse events

values.exp: 102/152 patients (67%); Table 3 totals 271 events (31 device-related, 240 therapy-related)

harms.locator: Full text, Safety, p 2031; Table 3, p 2032
harms.note: Table 3 lists new pain or undesired stimulation in 41/152 (27.0%), pain at PNE or the INS implant site in 29/152 (19.1%), and lead migration as device-related in 5/152 (3.3%) and therapy-related in 8/152 (5.3%). The abstract states 279 events, Results says 221, and Discussion says 271; Table 3 sums to 271. No life-threatening or irreversible events were reported.

harms.label: Adverse events requiring surgery
harms.locator: Full text, Safety, p 2031; Tables 3-4, pp 2032-2033
harms.note: Permanent explant for adverse event: 9/152 (5.9%) in Table 4; overall explant for adverse event or loss of efficacy: 16/152 (10.5%) in Safety.

delivery.label: Five-year cohort implantation
delivery.value: 17 centers enrolled 163 patients: 129 crossed over from MDT-103 and 34 enrolled under the new protocol; 11 of the latter declined implantation after positive testing, leaving 152 implants (96 urge incontinence, 25 urgency-frequency, 31 retention).
delivery.locator: Full text, Patient Selection and Evaluation, p 2030

delivery.label: Generator placement and diary follow-up
delivery.value: Generator placement was abdominal in 121/152 patients and buttock in 31/152; 105/152 completed the five-year visit and 87/152 a five-year diary. Missing diaries used last observation carried forward; adverse-event or efficacy withdrawals counted as failures.
delivery.locator: Full text, Patient Selection and Evaluation, Patient Disposition, and Statistical Analysis, p 2030; Table 1, p 2030
